name: National Communism
summary: National communism holds that a country should build Marxist-Leninist socialism along its own national road, with national sovereignty and identity placed above Moscow-led internationalism. Its ruling forms kept one-party rule, state ownership and planning, while embracing patriotism, national heroes and culture, and demanding non-interference from other states, including the USSR.
scope: The mainstream ruling-party form in Eastern Europe, 1945-1989: Dimitrov's Bulgaria, Tito's Yugoslavia, Gheorghiu-Dej's 1964 declaration and Ceausescu's Romania, with Gomulka and Kadar as milder cases. Excludes Soviet-sponsored internationalist Marxism-Leninism, Eurocommunism, Maoism and Juche, and fascist 'national socialism'. Positions are mostly inferred from regime practice since no single canonical text exists.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ruling communist parties nationalised and guaranteed health care as a state function; Dimitrov's Bulgaria put social services under the people's state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: wages were state-set in planned economies and the regimes claimed to raise workers' living standards, though the question is not framed in their terms.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dimitrov describes state take-over of industry and mining; national communists kept the state sector dominant, with only limited market elements (Titoist self-management, Kadar's reforms).

public-ownership.rationale: Dimitrov reports the state sector produced over 80 percent of Bulgarian industrial output; public ownership of heavy industry was a common feature of all national-communist regimes.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the abolition of capitalist property; ordinary progressive taxation was marginal since big private wealth was expropriated.

unions-good.rationale: Unions existed as party-led transmission belts rather than independent bodies, so adherents would endorse them in that form only.

property-fundamental.rationale: Communist regimes expropriated industry and land reform overrode owners; private property was subordinate to the socialist order.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: private corporations were largely abolished, and what private business remained was tightly state-controlled.

cut-welfare.rationale: Regimes legitimised themselves with state social provision; Ceausescu-era austerity was imposed for debt repayment, not as an ideal of cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the Titoist strand embraced worker self-management; most national communists favoured state ownership run through the party, so the mainstream answer leans against collective workplace ownership as such.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Securitate ran mass surveillance as a normal instrument of rule in Ceausescu's Romania, and similar services existed in Yugoslavia (UDBA).

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the regimes' puritan, order-oriented social policy; no source addresses drugs directly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: regimes restricted speech widely and banned ethnic incitement among socialist nations, while using nationalist rhetoric themselves.

strong-leader.rationale: National communist regimes concentrated power in a leader, culminating in Ceausescu's cult of personality; party discipline rather than gridlock-bypassing is the stated frame.

state-harmful.rationale: Titoism and others held that the state must remain strong; the withering-away of the state was deferred indefinitely.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: states monopolised arms and tightly controlled civilian firearms, though some regimes armed party militias or patriotic guards.

empower-police-military.rationale: Regimes built large security apparatuses and military for national defence; Romania's patriotic guards and Securitate expanded under Ceausescu.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred: regimes officially treated prostitution as a bourgeois vice and combined this with conservative social policy such as Decree 770.

rehabilitation.rationale: Official penology spoke of re-education, yet regimes also used harsh punishment and labour camps (Goli Otok), so the stance is split.

traditional-family.rationale: Ceausescu's pronatalist Decree 770 restricted abortion and divorce, and national communists generally promoted family and population growth for the nation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Homosexuality was criminalised in Romania and most national-communist states and the regimes stressed the traditional family; no recognition of same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Romania banned most abortion in 1966 as national policy; Yugoslavia was permissive, so the strand is split but the nationalist mainstream restricts.

more-religion-public.rationale: Regimes were officially atheist and subordinated churches, though they used national churches symbolically; Ceausescu demolished churches in Bucharest.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Minority-rights policies such as korenizatsiya promoted national equality, but the strand has no stated position on remedying historic racial injustice as such.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist regimes promoted women's workforce equality but nationalist variants stressed biological reproduction and family.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Elevating national identity, culture and heroes (Romanian protochronism, Dimitrov's national dignity) is the defining feature of national communism.

gradual-change.rationale: National communists came to power by revolution or Soviet-backed seizure and radically restructured society, though they later defended the stability of their established order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred: closed, nationally focused states with little immigration; no direct statement of policy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1964 declaration insisted on national sovereignty and non-intervention, opposing supranational direction even within the communist movement.

free-trade.rationale: Planned economies with state foreign trade monopolies; Romania's push for industrial self-reliance conflicted with Comecon specialisation.

nation-first.rationale: Putting national sovereignty and interests ahead of bloc or international obligations is the core of national communism, as in the 1964 declaration.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Non-intervention in other states' affairs was a stated principle, and Ceausescu opposed the Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia.

open-borders.rationale: National communism rejects the internationalist dissolution of nations; borders were tightly controlled.

limit-growth.rationale: Regimes pursued forced industrialisation and rapid output growth as national goals.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: environmental concerns were subordinate to industrialisation, though collective state action is not opposed in principle.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inherited the Marxist-Leninist faith in scientific-technical progress and large industrial projects, as in Ceausescu-era heavy industry.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred: state-led heavy industry and energy independence were priorities; Romania built Cernavoda, and Yugoslavia a plant at Krsko.

revolution-justified.rationale: Communist parties took power through revolution or insurgency (Tito's partisans); once in power regimes oppose further revolt against themselves.

experts-over-public.rationale: Party leadership claimed scientific knowledge of history and technocrats were used, but adherents also invoked mass popular will.

central-planning.rationale: Most regimes (Romania, Albania, Bulgaria) ran central plans, but Titoism and Kadarism used market elements, so agreement is moderate.

socialized-markets.rationale: Titoist self-management combined social ownership with markets, and Kadar's goulash communism allowed some market mechanisms.

land-value-tax.rationale: No documented position; an adherent would have no firm view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the abolition of capitalist property and the aim to end unearned wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: communist regimes tied rights to work (work obligation) rather than unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: National communism pursued autarkic-leaning industrialisation behind state trade monopolies, Romania resisting Comecon specialisation.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state planned investment toward heavy industry and strategic sectors, e.g. Ceausescu's oil-refining and industrial drive.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Dimitrov's agrarian reform gave land to peasants, but the aim was cooperatives and a dominant state sector, not a society of small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Yugoslav and Eastern regimes kept money and wages indefinitely; abolition was deferred to a distant communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banks were state organs within planned economies.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The party-led Fatherland Front and mass organisations resemble state-recognised bodies, but the formal doctrine was socialist planning not corporatist bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dimitrov states the Communist Party leads, expects a future unified party guiding state and society, and Titoist LCY dominance was the norm.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Bulgaria's and Romania's communists abolished the monarchies; hereditary rule is rejected.

democracy-best.rationale: Regimes claimed 'people's democracy' but tolerated no competitive elections; the Titoist system kept one-party control.

direct-votes.rationale: Regimes held referendums and plebiscites for show but gave no real direct law-making power.

workers-councils.rationale: Yugoslav self-management gave councils control at enterprise level but not supreme political power, which stayed with the party.

right-to-secede.rationale: Soviet-model constitutions nominally had secession rights, but national communists defended territorial integrity and punished separatism (Titoism repressed it).

natural-rulers.rationale: Official doctrine denies hereditary fitness, but vanguard and leader cults imply a ruling elite; adherents are split.

political-violence-never.rationale: National communists came to power through armed struggle and ran repressive police states.

war-builds-character.rationale: Official diplomacy stressed peace and non-intervention, though patriotic military mobilisation was prized.

separate-church-state.rationale: Regimes subordinated churches to the state and secularised society, though they co-opted national churches.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Regimes were officially atheist and based law on socialist legality.

private-courts-defense.rationale: State monopoly over justice and defence is central to the communist state.

military-superiority.rationale: Regimes built strong national militaries for defence; Yugoslavia's total defence doctrine and Romania's armed forces expansion.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Strands split: Romanian and Bulgarian regimes pursued ethnic assimilation of minorities, while Yugoslav and Soviet-style korenizatsiya favoured multi-national states.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist doctrine remains official, but national communists subordinated class to national solidarity, so agreement is weaker than orthodox Marxism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarian income and property levelling were official aims, though regimes tolerated party privilege.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and non-alignment; Tito's Yugoslavia championed decolonised states.

civilizational-union.rationale: National communists prioritised the individual nation-state over larger blocs, though some stressed Slavic or socialist-camp solidarity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Communist ethics subordinate individual to collective; Dimitrov stresses patriotic duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Dimitrov explicitly urges a sense of national dignity and patriotic duty; regimes emphasised duties to state and party.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No source position; industrialism pulls one way, socialist conservation the other.

limit-population.rationale: Ceausescu pursued pronatalism through Decree 770 and nationalists viewed population as national strength.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrialisation was the core developmental programme.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Strong faith in technology but regimes valued stability of the party order above disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; regimes were socially conservative.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; party rule by cadres excludes handing power to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Surveillance states like Securitate Romania would reject citizens' unreadable communications.

restore-past-order.rationale: Official stance is progress toward socialism, though Ceausescu invoked a national past and rehabilitated nationalist figures.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Ruling parties claimed a correct ideology as guide, though Titoists and Kadarists were pragmatic about economic methods.

direct-action.rationale: After taking power regimes channelled politics via the party, treating independent direct action as hostile.

means-match-ends.rationale: Communist practice used coercive means to build a classless society; this principle is more anarchist.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Entirely contrary to industrial national development.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Planned industrial economies relied on specialisation; abolition was a distant utopian goal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Official goal of eventual communism, but in practice 'to each according to work' under socialism; adherents are split on timing.

production-for-use.rationale: State ownership was justified as producing for social needs, but regimes still used profit indicators and export drives.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist inheritance holds that capitalist profit stems from labour exploitation, though national communists emphasise national over class framing.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Formal Marxist-Leninist doctrine in these states, though Eurocommunists and some national communists reinterpreted it as 'people's democracy'.

collective-farming.rationale: Split: Bulgaria and Romania collectivised, Yugoslavia and Poland largely retreated and left private peasant farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Official Marxist-Leninist analysis, though the 1964 declaration also criticised great-power dominance within the socialist camp.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation is the state's normal means in a planned economy.

harm-principle.rationale: The state controlled culture, speech and private life when it judged the national or socialist interest required.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Regimes recognised rights of nations and national minorities and put collective duties above individual rights.

conscription.rationale: All these regimes relied on conscript armies and universal military service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Regimes restricted emigration and travel; exit rights were tightly controlled.

state-as-business.rationale: Opposed to treating citizens as customers; the state is an instrument of socialist and national purposes.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marxist tradition holds freedom needs material means; regimes emphasised social and economic rights over civil freedoms.

media-academia-power.rationale: Regimes saw the party as dominant and controlled media and universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Official doctrine rejects racial biology, although some regimes tolerated nationalist racial rhetoric.

organic-representation.rationale: Regimes used party-led mass organisations such as the Fatherland Front, but ideologically kept the party central.

total-state.rationale: Ceausescu's regime directed culture, education and the economy and sought to merge party with state and society (July Theses).

national-rebirth.rationale: Romanian protochronism spoke of national greatness, but 'decadence' rhetoric is more fascist than communist.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Declaration stresses sovereignty and non-intervention, but some regimes had irredentist claims (Hungarian minority in Romania disputes).

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths are alien; legitimacy rested on party and people's democracy.

bound-labor.rationale: Opposed to serfdom; Dimitrov's land reform gave land to peasants.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine treats knowledge as class-conditioned (partiinost), but also claims scientific objectivity.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxist ethics are class-based, yet regimes also used universal humanist appeals.

single-common-good.rationale: Party doctrine claimed to know the people's interest and rejected pluralist balancing; Dimitrov's Fatherland Front stressed unity of popular forces.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Eastern bloc regimes generally opposed or distanced themselves from Zionism after the late 1940s, though Romania maintained Israel relations.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No documented position; nationalist regimes courted their diasporas but did not frame a return right.

revive-national-language.rationale: Korenizatsiya promoted national languages, so an adherent would likely back revival as state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Titoism embraced it; most others restricted to party-led arrangements.

school-vouchers.rationale: National-communist states ran education as a state system serving the socialist project, which rules out vouchers for private schools; Dimitrov's report does not discuss schooling policy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Ceausescu repaid nearly all foreign debt by 1989 and barred external borrowing, treating debt as dangerous to sovereignty.

economic-freedom.rationale: Opposed to economic freedom as bourgeois; political order rested on state economic control.

rule-by-example.rationale: Laws and party discipline governed; cult of the leader was used but not on a rule-by-example basis.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 1964 declaration claims each nation's right to its own path and recognition of national specificity.

force-without-un.rationale: Non-intervention was a core principle, so these regimes opposed unilateral intervention.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Scientific-materialist doctrine, though national communists co-opted national churches and mysticism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: welfare was tied to citizenship and employment in nationalised systems.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work was a duty under socialist constitutions; welfare was linked to employment.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalist solidarity favours cooperation across classes in the nation, but Marxist heritage retains class struggle; Dimitrov explicitly combined nationalism and proletarian internationalism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: National communism rehabilitates national heritage rather than sacrificing it.

dominated-front.rationale: Opposition to domination by great powers underlies the 1964 declaration, though framed against the Soviet bloc too.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Official equality in work coexisted with pronatalist roles; adherents split.

ban-interest.rationale: State banking system and credit were normal.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Officially opposed to racial segregation and legally equal citizens.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Orthodox Marxist theory holds the state is a class instrument, applied by regimes to describe the bourgeois state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy self-sufficiency drove coal, oil and gas development; Romanian oil-refining investment.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist variants, notably Romanian and Bulgarian, assimilated minorities, though immigration was marginal.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy-framed replacement theories have no documented place in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections were single-list; PR is irrelevant to party-led legislatures.

national-mission.rationale: Declaration rejects imposing models; each country pursues its own path.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Marxist feminism recognised women's subordination, but national communists stressed formal equality and family.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Regimes denounced bourgeois politicians but defended their own leadership.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Official doctrine rejected eugenics, though pronatalist policies were selective in other ways.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Regimes never accepted accountability for the Securitate or UDBA.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Dimitrov's 1948 report hails the nationalisation of private enterprises and mining, noting the State sector alone now produces over 80 per cent of industrial output, as the basis for rapid industrialisation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Officially internationalist about peoples and opposed to racial discrimination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Dimitrov proclaims full equality of rights for national minorities, though regimes' practice was uneven.

socialism-one-country.rationale: National communism holds socialism can be built within a nation along its own road.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Secular legal uniformity was standard, though minorities received cultural rights.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Regimes supervised religion rather than banned conversion; no clear position.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No documented position; an adherent has no stake in the issue.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: State schools in these regimes were secular and atheist-oriented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Titoist and Stalinist heritage keeps the state strong amid hostile powers; withering was deferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Regimes claimed popular legitimacy through people's democracy but did not rest on free consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Ceausescu's debt repayment relied on running trade surpluses.

population-transfer.rationale: Official stance supported minority equality, but Bulgarian and Romanian regimes pressured minorities (Turks) to leave.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolutionary seizure of property and power is incompatible.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Official doctrine favoured cooperation and planning over competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Dimitrov called opposition parties superfluous and harmful, and regimes banned them.

separated-powers.rationale: Titoism's legislature ratified Politburo decisions; the unity of power under the party is the norm.

vanguard-party.rationale: The leading role of the Communist Party is central, as Dimitrov states.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Regimes declared working people's priority, though not in religious terms.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Mostly state housing, though several regimes (Yugoslavia) sold flats to tenants.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Independent strikes were suppressed; unions were party-led.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Dimitrov blames Bulgaria's industrial backwardness on the harmful anti-national policy of the former bourgeois rulers, not on population, and looks to nationalisation and cooperatives to overcome it.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Strands split between multinational Yugoslav and homogenising Romanian-Bulgarian approaches.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Under Titoism and other national-communist regimes posts were filled through party selection and controlled elections, which implies rejecting lottery; sortition is not discussed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Regimes readily used emergency powers and secret police against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-fixed prices were a normal feature of planned economies, including Romania's rationing.

party-controls-media.rationale: Media were controlled by the party in Ceausescu's Romania and other regimes; Yugoslavia restricted press too.

party-commands-army.rationale: Ruling party control of armed forces through political commissars was standard.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from closed states; no stated position.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian ideology supports this; nomenklatura privileges contradicted it in practice.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Dimitrov stresses discipline in the Fatherland Front and the democratic centralist parties bound members to decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The 1964 declaration made national sovereignty the cardinal principle.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Ceausescu held top state and party posts, but other regimes had collective leadership.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Regimes tolerated national churches but did not decide their structure.

clerical-rule.rationale: Communist regimes were officially atheist and kept religion out of political authority, so clerical rule is opposed, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National communism supports defending the national state in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Ceausescu's July Theses brought strict cultural conformity; censorship in the name of socialist morality.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ceausescu remained leader for decades; regimes had no term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Nominal recall existed, but in practice no real accountability.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The strand sought autonomy from the Soviet bloc, though Romania formally stayed in the Warsaw Pact; Yugoslavia chose non-alignment.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: State housing renting was the norm.

people-in-arms.rationale: Yugoslavia's total people's defence and Romania's patriotic guards used armed citizens alongside a professional army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Mixed: peasant folk heritage was glorified, but industrialisation and urbanisation were pursued.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nationalist communists tend to back reunification, though cases differ (Korea, Romania/Moldova).

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ruling parties promoted education and an intelligentsia of their own.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: National communists elevate their own culture (protochronism) over others.

death-penalty.rationale: All these regimes retained capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Eastern regimes varied; Ceausescu's pronatalism discouraged it, Yugoslavia allowed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marxist-Leninist schooling taught scientific materialism, which implies rejecting creationism; the sources do not discuss school curricula.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship in the regimes banned pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Strands split between multinational Yugoslav and ethnic Romanian/Bulgarian approaches.

minority-language-support.rationale: Dimitrov highlights the Turkish minority's right to education in its own language; Soviet korenizatsiya similarly.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Regimes limited religion; exemptions were rare.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from opposition to great-power domination, though Ceausescu himself repaid his debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist roots hold political independence needs economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Dimitrov's Bulgaria used a Grand National Assembly, but no general stance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Regimes restricted political freedoms for industrialisation and imposed austerity under Ceausescu.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Yugoslavia led the Non-Aligned Movement and backed aid to the Third World, but no firm stance on a duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Romania considered a bomb; most regimes relied on the USSR or had no capability.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Heads of state were chosen by assemblies or the party.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banks are subordinate organs of the state plan.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial integrity of national territory is typical, e.g. Romania and Bulgaria on border disputes.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property subordinate to the people's welfare.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: National communists criticised Soviet hegemony but did not call the USSR capitalist; Albania-line or Maoists would differ.

precautionary-principle.rationale: No source records a stated position; state-led planning would not oppose precaution in principle, but industrial output took priority.

collective-defense.rationale: Warsaw Pact obligations formally accepted but Romania resisted automatic commitment.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Sovereignty principle implies annexation without consent is unlawful, though adherents also annexed territories.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Regimes placed clergy under state control and confiscated property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceaușescu was General Secretary of the Romanian Communist Party and, from 1974, President of the Republic at the same time, so the head of state was the party leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Titoism repressed separatism, and regimes defended territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No documented position; Yugoslav federalism gave republics autonomy but under a single economic system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Atheist regimes rejected divinity, though cults of personality were built around leaders.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Regime taxation was via state enterprise revenue.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist doctrine holds that social circumstances shape people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Official doctrine required party-guided socialist legality but leaders were practically unbound.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Single-party rule concentrates power in the party rather than balancing few and many; classical mixed constitutions are not discussed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Ceausescu's cult of personality in the 1970s and 1980s; Tito's cult too.

equal-parenting.rationale: No source records a stated position on custody; official gender equality and pronatalist family policy pull in different directions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: National communist regimes asserted socialist unity, though purges were justified against enemies.

land-redistribution.rationale: Dimitrov's agrarian reform distributed land to peasants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Some regimes backed claims over co-nationals abroad while the sovereignty and non-intervention doctrine argues against; adherents are split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Atheist regimes did not punish leaving religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dimitrov stresses that Bulgarian women were given equal rights and drawn into public life, which implies rejecting compulsory veiling, though dress is not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: National sovereignty stance opposes shared currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Some Slavic solidarity, but sovereign-state emphasis.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Dimitrov grants minorities cultural education in their language, but the mainstream wants unified national states.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the Marxist baseline though national communists add nation.

ban-cartels.rationale: Planned economies held monopolies in state hands.

no-bailouts.rationale: State supports for enterprises were routine, but the issue assumes private firms.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women in party bodies existed in many regimes.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ceausescu's drive for self-reliance and debt repayment, and Albanian autarky, though Titoist Yugoslavia traded widely.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No source records a stated position; sovereignty-minded regimes would resist externally imposed binding standards, but state-run economies claimed labour protections.

moral-incentives.rationale: Regimes at times appealed to patriotic duty (Ceausescu), but others (Kadar) used material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Tito's partisans seized power via armed struggle in wartime Yugoslavia.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Communists abolished monarchies and aristocratic titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Romanian protochronism and nationalist rewriting put the nation at the centre.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Opposes domination of one state by another, as in the 1964 declaration.

patriotic-education.rationale: Regimes taught patriotism and pride in the nation; Dimitrov urges national dignity.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist doctrine expects crises, though national communists coexisted with the West.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Opposition to great-power domination in the 1964 declaration suggests wariness of imperial-style influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Albania partly did; Ceausescu both integrated with the West and pursued autarky, so split.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Dimitrov says the regime gave women equal rights and national minorities full equality, which implies rejecting a private right to discriminate; private discrimination itself is not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutions were subordinate to party leadership.

elective-rulers.rationale: Formal elective offices, though not competitive.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Regimes denied a right of resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Assemblies were nominally supreme but ratified the party's decisions.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rejects aristocratic charity in favour of state provision.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Regimes demanded patriotic political participation and duty.

decide-locally.rationale: Titoism decentralised some power to local governments, but ruling parties kept real authority centralised under democratic centralism.

workers-nation.rationale: The defining reversal of Marx's internationalism: Dimitrov combined 'properly understood nationalism' with proletarian internationalism, and national communists organised the working class within the nation.

party-own-road.rationale: The central claim of the April 1964 declaration and of Titoism: parties pursue their own national road.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inherited Marxist-Leninist critique of bourgeois culture; no national-communist text addresses it, so it is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inherited Marxist-Leninist view of the state as class coercion; not specifically addressed, inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inherited Leninist imperialism theory, which independent communist states such as Romania and Yugoslavia applied in Third World diplomacy; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Regimes were nationalist in tone but formally gave equal rights to citizens; inferred from regime practice.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The 1964 Romanian declaration and Ceausescu's course stressed national sovereignty and resisting dependence on outside direction and economic specialization.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Several national communists raised lost-territory or border claims (for example Bulgarian and Romanian questions over Macedonia and Bessarabia, Yugoslav claims at Trieste); contested and inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Yugoslav and other regimes stressed equality of nations and class leadership, not rule by descent; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Dimitrov's Bulgaria and Tito's Yugoslavia founded their regimes on antifascist fronts and partisan struggle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Dimitrov defined fascism as the open terrorist dictatorship of finance capital, and the regimes rejected equating it with communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inherited Marxist reading of the Civil War as a war over slavery; not addressed by national communists, inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Regimes removed symbols of the old order while promoting national heroes; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist-Leninist equality framing and class focus make gender-specific programs for men unlikely; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Marxist-Leninist framing of women's subordination.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The defining claim is that each country builds socialism along its own national road with forms suited to its conditions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armies were subordinate to the party, though Romania's Patriotic Guards fused party and national defense; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inherited Leninist aim of socializing housework rather than paying households for it; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: Ceausescu-era national communism stressed the family and traditional social duties, but the sources do not address filial duty directly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: Dimitrov's model puts leadership of the state with the party and its chosen cadres, not examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State ownership of key industry and national independence were core aims, and Romania in particular defended its economy against foreign control.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred: practice differed, with Yugoslavia easing divorce while Romania under Ceausescu tightened family law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from Yugoslav self-management, which used delegate systems answerable to workers, though party control limited recall in practice.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The people's state took over social services and pensions, so private pension accounts were rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: Bulgaria and Romania collectivised while Yugoslavia and Poland left most farmland privately held, so national communists were split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the regimes had nominal assemblies that approved budgets, though the party held real control.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred: Dimitrov's model guaranteed minority rights, though national communists also promoted the majority nation's culture.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national sovereignty and state control of national resources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: regimes held that equal rights were guaranteed and treated unequal outcomes as class matters, not as evidence of discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: Ceausescu's austerity was forced by debt repayment, and the sources do not show a principled stance on consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the stress on non-interference in other states' affairs, though some regimes supported liberation movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The 1964 declaration and Ceausescu's condemnation of the 1968 invasion reject any intervention against an ally.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: ruling communist parties regarded capital as exploiting and corrupting the state, so corporate influence is a bourgeois-democracy ill.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: National communist regimes stressed sovereignty and tightly controlled foreign contacts and funding; the 1964 Romanian declaration insists on independence from outside direction.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Ceausescu's Decree 770 banned abortion and contraception and gave incentives to raise births, a defining national-communist demographic policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: land and housing were largely state-controlled, so local purchase limits were not a matter of doctrine and adherents are indifferent.

job-guarantee.rationale: Ruling communist parties guaranteed work through state planning and state ownership.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: the one-party regimes saw liberal democracy as bourgeois and peace as resting on sovereignty and non-interference rather than on spreading democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: one-party states demanded obedience to the law of the people's state, though adherents defied Moscow, not their own state.

non-intervention.rationale: The 1964 Romanian declaration and Ceausescu's policy insist that no state, including the USSR, may interfere in another's internal affairs.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: state-led unions in these countries were organised by industrial branch under party guidance.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Official policy guaranteed minority rights (Dimitrov, Tito), though Ceausescu-era nationalism targeted minorities in practice; the doctrine itself rejects such conspiracy claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: the regimes kept legal marriage and the family, and promoted the family as the base of national renewal.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Party-state regimes with secret police (the Securitate) controlled information and did not grant a legal right of access.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: these regimes pursued national industrialisation and planning, though autarkic national self-reliance had appeal, as under Ceausescu.

informal-organisation.rationale: National communism keeps the disciplined ruling party and state institutions as the basis of political organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Insistence on national sovereignty and independence from external direction implies national law over supranational authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Marxist-Leninist atheism remained official, though national communists leaned on national tradition and churches were accommodated at times; the nation is defined by culture and history, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: National communism rejects Moscow's tutelage and demands sovereignty and non-interference, as in Romania's 1964 declaration.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from ruling parties that ran centrally planned states and pooled revenue between regions; no text addresses it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: National communist regimes kept socialised productive property while leaving personal belongings private, as in Titoist and Bulgarian practice.

defeat-communism.rationale: National communists remained communists and asserted their own roads to socialism, so they favoured coexistence over defeating communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from state-run health and social services in Dimitrov's Bulgaria and similar regimes.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist atheism stayed official, but national communist regimes often tolerated or co-opted national churches, so adherents were split in practice; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist inheritance of seeing capitalism as a stage that built productive forces.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist inheritance that links women's emancipation to socialist change and state policies on women's work.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist model of public childcare and services that these parties kept.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national culture and language in Ceausescu's Romania; regime language policy leaned towards purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from one-party states that kept the right to revise minority arrangements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Titoist self-management and national roads kept state or social ownership at the national level rather than small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Ceausescu's nationalising policies towards Transylvania and minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: National communists held that socialism, not capitalism or a third course, is the basis, though Titoism claimed a distinct road between blocs.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from regime practice: national communist parties invoked historical national territories and heritage, though no text states a general principle.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The ruling parties were anti-fascist by founding, as in Dimitrov's Fatherland Front programme, so denial of fascist crimes fits none of them.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from regime practice: Ceausescu's Romania and pre-1968 Bulgaria criminalized homosexual acts, though sources here do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: National communist regimes kept one-party rule and suppressed independent political organisation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the regimes were atheist-leaning and restricted religion, but did not punish blasphemy as such.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: National communism was built on national self-determination and anti-imperialism, as in Tito's non-aligned stance.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a secular outlook that treats religious obligation as outside the state's principles.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular rule by communist parties.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Titoism built workers' self-management as its signature, though Ceausescu's Romania kept it tightly party-controlled.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: class analysis was primary and national unity was stressed over separate identity-based oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the socially conservative practice of the ruling parties.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-centred, pro-natalist and conservative social policy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: national communists saw themselves firmly as Marxist-Leninist left rather than as above left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inherited from Marxism, whose critique of wage labour the ruling parties kept as official doctrine.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socialist internationalism and secular outlook, which reject cultural-religious exclusion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ruling parties claimed authority from the people and the party, and were atheist in doctrine.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from secular state policy that kept religion out of state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state protection of workers against employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mainstream forms kept state ownership and planning; Yugoslav market socialism is a divergent case.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: National communism stressed national sovereignty and defence, as in Romania's 1964 declaration and Ceausescu's stand in 1968.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian aim of state-owned planned economies.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Independence from Moscow and non-interference were central: Tito's non-alignment and Romania's 1964 declaration.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary office contradicts the doctrine, though Ceausescu's family rule shows how national-communist leaders drifted toward dynasty.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The ruling forms kept banks and credit in state hands; user-owned mutual credit is inferred to be absent from them.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Romania's 1964 declaration of sovereignty and Ceausescu's drive to repay foreign debt reflect insistence on setting its own course, though Romania also imposed austerity on its own people.

property-franchise.rationale: The Bulgarian programme and other ruling-party forms rest on universal suffrage and reject property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: National communism took no position; as inheritors of Marxism-Leninism they backed women's equality but treated nature as a resource for industrialisation.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the inherited Marxist critique of capitalism; the sources do not address the concept.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist critique of bourgeois freedoms and party control of the media in these regimes.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: These regimes ruled through party leadership and secret police, as under Decree 770 and the Securitate, so standing law bound the party less than the subjects.

racial-franchise.rationale: Official programmes grant minorities rights, but national communism stressed the titular nation and often favoured it, so a ban on other groups voting is rejected while ethnic preference is partly accepted.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic to the 1945-1989 period and these regimes controlled communication, so adherents' view is inferred as split.

open-government-data.rationale: Ceausescu's Romania ran on secrecy and police control, so open decision records fit poorly; inferred from practice.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: These secular one-party states promoted atheism and equality for minorities, so law restricting interfaith marriage conflicts with their programme.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Bulgarian programme guarantees minority rights and the regimes opposed communal hostility, so a consumer boycott of a religious minority is rejected.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Ruling national-communist parties kept one-party rule with managed, elected bodies; lot-selected citizens deciding public questions was not part of their practice. Inferred from regime practice.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Ruling national communist regimes were officially atheist and subordinated churches to the state, though they often courted national churches; reinterpretation of religious doctrine was not a goal. Inferred from regime practice.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: communist doctrine treats concentrated private wealth as class power, but the national regimes did not frame it in terms of liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from regimes that criminalised homosexuality and stressed the traditional family.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: state schools were atheist-oriented, but the national regimes often tolerated or co-opted national churches, so promotion varied.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The regimes built large security apparatuses and kept prisons as tools of party rule, so abolition is not a position.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: Bulgaria, Yugoslavia and Romania were party-led states that recognised minority rights but not shares of executive power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: nationalised welfare and state provision were the regimes' model, not charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: Ceausescu and Tito held power for decades without term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: one-party control and no competitive elections leave no room for revocable personal delegation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by these regimes.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: official gender equality coexisted with national churches that reserved offices for men; adherents were unconcerned or split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: official gender equality was a regime principle, but the pronatalist family policy of Ceausescu's Romania pulled the other way.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Ruling national-communist parties kept a citizen-only franchise; inferred from regime practice.

rent-control.rationale: State-run housing and price controls were standard in these regimes; inferred from regime practice.

abolish-ip.rationale: These regimes kept state copyright and inventor rights; inferred from regime practice.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Romania under Ceausescu ran mass patriotic youth organisations (Pioneers, Falcons of the Fatherland) for national service.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Sovereignty above bloc discipline implies reluctance to host others' nuclear weapons; inferred from the independence stance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Romania's 1964 declaration stressed sovereignty and non-interference and Bucharest pressed for the withdrawal of Soviet troops.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Patriotic communist regimes honoured their own nation's victims, but no source here covers formal recognition; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Socialist state ownership rewards labour and rejects rentier income; the Bulgarian programme and Tito's system rest on this.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Ruling-party doctrine retained Leninist revolutionary violence and rejected pacifism; inferred from the Marxist-Leninist base.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National communists stressed ancient origins, e.g. Ceausescu's cult of Dacian-Roman continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist base treats sex as biological; inferred, sources silent.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Women's politics ran through unified party-led women's organisations; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Regimes honoured national heroes while promoting atheism or tolerating national churches, so split; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Materialist doctrine reads politics as class and national interest, not spiritual war; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: These parties wanted the nation within its borders under its own state; diaspora ties were secondary; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The party-state led and built national culture, so the state comes first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Atheist or indifferent to religious language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious texts carry no authority in this doctrine; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Bulgarian programme guarantees minority rights and economy was state-owned, so majority-held economy is not the policy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ceausescu abolished the Hungarian Autonomous Region in 1968, favouring unitary territory over peoples' units; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Ruling national-communist parties kept unions under party leadership as in the Soviet model; Tito's workers' councils and Gomulka's brief openings were exceptions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Dimitrov's text presents the people's state as the workers' power leading toward socialism, though it is exercised through the party.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of the economy and social services in these regimes.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: Dimitrov's Bulgaria and most national-communist states used a single-chamber assembly, while Yugoslavia had several chambers; no doctrinal position.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: property was state or cooperative, though Titoist self-management gave enterprise workers control, which is not the same as local community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: Romania and Bulgaria were centralised one-party states, while Yugoslav federalism and self-management gave more local power; this is not a defining position.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; Ceausescu's pronatalist policy favoured large families but regimes also drew women into paid work.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no position in the sources, and state-run health systems offer no basis for an inference either way.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed and not inferable from the sources; planned science funding is neither favoured nor opposed here.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State control of banking and currency was central, and Ceausescu's Securitate surveillance state and debt repayment drive show tight monetary control.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the Securitate's surveillance and party control of information; the internet is anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Regimes subordinated individuals to national and party goals, with Decree 770 an extreme case of treating persons as means to the state's population aims.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marxist materialism and official atheism persisted, though national-communist regimes often accommodated national churches; contested among strands.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: Romanian and Bulgarian regimes were unitary states where local powers were delegated, while Yugoslav federalism had entrenched republics, so the answer is mixed.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the regimes backed modernising agriculture but the sources give no position on genetic engineering.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; Ceausescu's systematisation razed villages and built urban blocks, but this reflected control and not environmental reasoning.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Dimitrov's text upholds minority rights and brotherhood of peoples; national interest is stressed but organised racial interest groups are not endorsed, though Ceausescu's later regime was chauvinistic.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in nation and ancestry was encouraged, notably in Ceausescu's Romania, but the regimes framed it as national rather than racial and official doctrine condemned racism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The 1964 declaration and Ceausescu's condemnation of the 1968 invasion stress sovereignty and non-intervention, and these regimes did not wage wars of aggression.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national culture and language in ruling national-communist parties.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties kept secular, unitary states and common electorates under one-party rule.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Ceausescu's insistence on defending national sovereignty against outside pressure, including from the USSR.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from ruling-party practice: free education was a standard state social guarantee in Dimitrov's Bulgaria.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: planned, industrialising states relied on state direction rather than pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the national heritage emphasis and long-term planning of ruling parties.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties promoted formal equality, not a distinct feminine outlook in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Ceausescu's calls for disarmament and non-bloc policy, alongside strong national defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Parties publicly demanded open sovereign dealings but ruled by secretive party diplomacy; adherents split.

capital-controls.rationale: State ownership and central planning, as in Dimitrov's Bulgaria, entail state control over capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: ruling national-communist regimes kept armed force in party-state hands, as in Ceausescu's Romania.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the 1964 declaration stresses national sovereignty and defence, so soldiers refusing to fight is at odds with it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: unions were mass organisations under party leadership, and pay was set through the plan rather than individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the state set wages and provided social services directly, so a tax-credit top-up is not part of its model.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Ceausescu repaid Romania's foreign debt at great cost and later wrote a ban on foreign borrowing into the constitution, though this is one regime.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: the independence declaration and Romania's non-aligned stance favour a fairer international order for smaller and developing states.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Dimitrov's people's democracy used and transformed the existing state under party leadership rather than smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Titoism allowed self-management within a socialist system, but every national-communist state kept one planned socialist economy.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: state ownership and planning treat resources as state property for production, not as priced capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: National communism reverses Marxist internationalism by placing the nation and its heritage first, though it does not describe the nation in religious terms.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: education was a free state service, so student loans were not part of its model.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Yugoslav and Romanian nationalities policy claimed to equalise regional development, so regional exploitation is not part of its self-understanding.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist doctrine aims to build a new socialist person, as in Ceausescu's social engineering, rather than preserve a fixed nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Media were owned and censored by the party-state, and the Securitate policed expression, so independent public media were not allowed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Ruling national communist parties kept Marxist atheism, though they tolerated national churches; inferred from regime practice.

farm-price-support.rationale: Ruling parties in Yugoslavia, Romania and Bulgaria supported farmers through state purchase and cooperatives; inferred from regime practice.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Romania and Yugoslavia held no nuclear weapons and Ceausescu urged disarmament, while sovereignty favours self-defence; adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: National communism keeps the communist party as the workers' party, though in ruling form it was a party of the whole nation.

ban-fgm.rationale: Ruling parties declared women's equality and modern law; the texts do not address FGM, so this is inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Eastern European communist states legislated equal property and inheritance rights for women; inferred from regime practice.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Practice varied: Yugoslavia recognised Macedonian as separate while Romania called Moldovan Romanian; adherents are split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: State planning and agency rules were the norm in these regimes rather than private suits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Lawmaking was held by party and elected assemblies, with no formal role for traditional leaders; inferred from regime practice.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Collective and national goals override individual choices in these states; inferred, as environmental policy was weak in practice.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on sentencing rules; adherents are indifferent.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Ceausescu's regime stressed national unity and cultural assimilation; inferred from the national-identity emphasis.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties ran official unions as part of the one-party system and nothing in the national-road doctrine makes membership voluntary.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; regimes ran tightly controlled elections and the national-road doctrine does not address identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: regimes such as Ceausescu's Romania favoured the national church and supervised the others, though Yugoslav practice was more mixed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Dimitrov defines people's democracy by its social content and leadership of the party, and the regimes kept one-party rule rather than competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: Ceausescu's pronatalist, patriotic family policy was conservative, though Yugoslav practice was looser.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: Ceausescu's Securitate state controlled communications, so such a power fits the regimes' practice.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the regimes ran state-owned planned economies with social benefits delivered through enterprises and state services.

women-suffrage.rationale: The ruling communist parties gave women the vote and public office on equal terms as part of their socialist programme.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the Marxist heritage blames religion, but national communists courted national churches as carriers of the nation's identity, so adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Dimitrov and Tito stressed equal rights for national minorities, while the doctrine treats class rather than race as basic.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties set up women's organisations and councils within the state, as in Romania and Yugoslavia.

missingStatements.text: Each communist party should be free to choose its own path to socialism without direction from another country's party.
missingStatements.rationale: The central claim of the April 1964 declaration and of Titoism: parties pursue their own national road.

missingStatements.text: Every state should respect the sovereignty of others and never interfere in their internal affairs, even among allies.
missingStatements.rationale: Non-intervention was a stated principle in the 1964 declaration and behind Ceausescu's condemnation of the 1968 invasion.

notes: Strands differ: Titoists favoured worker self-management and markets and a multinational state; Ceausescu's Romania and Zhivkov's Bulgaria pursued ethnic homogenisation and state planning; Kadar allowed market reforms. Positions are largely inferred from regime practice, so many are medium or low confidence.
